brief.setting: Colorectal outpatient clinic, on a rectal examination manikin
brief.scenario: Mr Leonard Pryce, 55, has had 2 months of fresh blood mixed with his stool and a feeling of incomplete emptying. Your consultant has asked you to perform a rigid sigmoidoscopy and proctoscopy in clinic. A rigid sigmoidoscope, proctoscope, light source, insufflation bulb, lubricant, gloves and biopsy forceps are provided.
brief.task: Perform the examination on the manikin, talking the examiner through each step, and answer questions.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Consent and chaperone, position, inspect and DRE, proctoscope, sigmoidoscope under vision, findings, aftercare.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Passing an instrument before a rectal examination, or advancing the scope blind.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'll explain the test, ask for his consent and offer a chaperone."

grid.label: Consent
grid.fail: Starts without explaining the test or asking permission.
grid.pass: Explains the test and gains consent: some discomfort and wind, a possible painless biopsy, and a little bleeding afterwards.
grid.high: Adds the rare serious risks: heavier bleeding, and perforation (5 in 328,815 rigid sigmoidoscopies in a UK survey); invites questions.

grid.label: Chaperone and dignity
grid.fail: Doesn't offer a chaperone, or leaves him exposed.
grid.pass: Offers a chaperone before starting; privacy to undress and keeps him covered.
grid.high: Tells him he can ask to stop at any time; records consent, the chaperone discussion and who was present.

grid.label: Equipment and position
grid.fail: Can't assemble the scope, or examines him lying on his back.
grid.pass: Checks the light, obturator, eyepiece and bellows; left lateral, hips and knees flexed.
grid.high: Tests the light and insufflation before starting; has biopsy forceps and specimen pots ready.

grid.label: Inspection and DRE first (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Passes an instrument without inspecting the anus or doing a rectal examination.
grid.pass: Parts the buttocks and inspects; then a digital rectal examination with a lubricated finger before any instrument.
grid.high: Doesn't instrument if the DRE suggests anal stenosis, an abscess or perforation; stops and seeks senior advice instead.

grid.label: Proctoscopy
grid.fail: Inserts without the obturator, or looks only on the way in.
grid.pass: Lubricated proctoscope inserted fully with the obturator held in; removes the obturator; inspects the canal while withdrawing slowly.
grid.high: Rotates or reinserts to see the whole circumference; biopsies only above the dentate line.

grid.label: Rigid sigmoidoscopy under vision (safety-critical)
grid.fail: Pushes the scope blindly or against resistance.
grid.borderline: Advances under vision but doesn't insufflate, so keeps pushing into the rectal wall.
grid.pass: Inserts with the obturator towards the umbilicus, removes it, insufflates gently and advances only under direct vision.
grid.high: Angles posteriorly as the rectum follows the sacrum; never forces past the rectosigmoid; notes how far the scope reached.

grid.label: Findings and biopsy
grid.fail: Doesn't inspect on withdrawal, or can't say where the lesion is.
grid.pass: Inspects the mucosa while withdrawing under vision; records each lesion's distance from the anal verge and wall position; biopsies it.
grid.high: Explains that the height from the anal verge (low, mid or high rectum) guides rectal cancer treatment planning.

grid.label: Aftercare and record
grid.fail: Leaves without explaining the findings or recording the examination.
grid.pass: Explains what was seen; warns of a little bleeding after a biopsy; says how he will get the results.
grid.high: Tells him honestly the lesion needs urgent tests and the colorectal team; documents findings, distances, biopsies and the chaperone.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Asks him to lie on his back and starts opening the scope without explaining.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Doesn't mention a chaperone; leaves him uncovered.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Inserts the proctoscope straight away without a rectal examination.]

fail.text: [Pushes the proctoscope in without the obturator and looks only on the way in.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Pushes the sigmoidoscope in against resistance without looking.]

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: Somewhere in the rectum, I think.

fail.speaker: candidate
fail.text: [Removes the scope and leaves without explaining or writing anything.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Mr Pryce, I'd like to look inside your back passage with a short tube. It may feel uncomfortable and windy; I may take a painless sample, and you may bleed a little afterwards. Are you happy to go ahead?

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Would you like a chaperone? [Gives privacy to undress and covers him.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Checks the light, obturator, eyepiece and bellows.] Please lie on your left side with your hips and knees bent.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Parts the buttocks and inspects, then a lubricated digital rectal examination.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inserts the lubricated proctoscope fully with the obturator held in, removes it, and inspects the canal while withdrawing slowly.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inserts the sigmoidoscope towards the umbilicus, removes the obturator, attaches the eyepiece, insufflates gently and advances only when the lumen is seen.]

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: [Inspects while withdrawing.] Ulcerated lesion on the posterior wall, lower edge 7 cm from the anal verge. I'll biopsy it.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: I've seen an area that needs testing and have taken samples. You may bleed a little, and I'll make sure you get the results.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: I'd like to look inside your back passage with a short tube. It may feel windy, and any sample is painless. You may bleed a little afterwards. Very rarely there is heavier bleeding or a tear in the bowel wall. Any questions?

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Would you like a chaperone? You can ask me to stop at any time. [Covers him; records his consent and that the clinic nurse is chaperoning.]

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Tests the light and insufflation first; biopsy forceps and pots ready.] Left side, knees bent, please.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects, then DRE.] If this were very painful, stenosed or felt like an abscess, I'd stop and get senior advice rather than pass a scope.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Proctoscope in with the obturator held, obturator out, withdraws slowly and rotates to see the whole circumference.] I'd only biopsy above the dentate line.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Towards the umbilicus, obturator out, eyepiece on, gentle air, then angles back as the rectum follows the sacrum, advancing only under vision.] I won't force past the rectosigmoid, and I'll note how far I reached.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: [Inspects on withdrawal.] Ulcerated, friable lesion on the posterior wall, lower edge 7 cm from the anal verge, so mid rectum. That height guides treatment planning. I'll biopsy it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Mr Pryce, I've found an area that looks abnormal and taken samples. It needs urgent further tests, and you'll see the colorectal team quickly. [Documents findings, distance, biopsies and chaperone.]

failures.move: Passing the proctoscope or sigmoidoscope without inspecting the anus and doing a rectal examination.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: a stenosis, abscess or tumour is met blind, causing pain or injury.

failures.move: Advancing the rigid sigmoidoscope without seeing the lumen.
failures.consequence: Safety-critical: risks perforating the rectum or rectosigmoid.

failures.move: Not offering a chaperone, or not recording the discussion.
failures.consequence: Breaches GMC guidance for an intimate examination.

failures.move: Not recording the lesion's distance from the anal verge and its position.
failures.consequence: The height that guides rectal cancer surgery is lost.

recovery.line: I'll withdraw a little, add some air and re-angle before going any further.
Before any instrument, I'll inspect and do a rectal examination.

knowledge.fact: Inspect and do a rectal examination before any instrument. Insert towards the umbilicus, then angle back; insufflate and advance only under vision; inspect on withdrawal.
Don't pass an instrument if the examination suggests a stenosis, an abscess or a perforation; stop and get senior advice.
UK survey: perforation in 5 of 328,815 rigid sigmoidoscopies; significant bleeding in 35.
Tumour height is measured from the anal verge by rigid rectoscopy: UICC low up to 6 cm, mid 6–12 cm, high 12–16 cm.
Explain, allow questions, say he can ask to stop; record consent; offer a chaperone and record the discussion.

recall.think: Perforation, a missed rectal cancer, an examination without consent.
recall.say: "Rectal examination first; I only advance what I can see."
do: Scope under vision; inspect on withdrawal; biopsy

numbers.meaning: upper limits of low, mid and high rectum from the anal verge (UICC)

recall.trap: Blood on the glove isn't proof of haemorrhoids: look higher.
recall.finish: Findings with distance recorded, biopsies sent, urgent colorectal follow-up.

sources.name: GMC: Intimate examinations and chaperones
sources.version: In effect from 30 January 2024; updated 13 December 2024
sources.supports: Explain why the examination is needed and what it involves, give a chance to ask questions, and explain the patient can ask at any time for it to stop (para 8); obtain consent and record it (para 9); privacy to undress and keep covered (para 12); offer a chaperone wherever possible (para 16); record the chaperone discussion and its outcome (para 23)

sources.name: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery (O'Connell, McCaskie, Sayers, eds)
sources.supports: Proctoscopy and rigid sigmoidoscopy technique: left lateral position; inspection and digital rectal examination before any instrument; obturator in on insertion, removed for viewing; insufflation and advancing only under vision; inspection on withdrawal; biopsy above the dentate line, where the mucosa is insensitive; stop if the examination suggests stenosis, abscess or perforation

sources.name: Robinson RJ, Stone M, Mayberry JF. Sigmoidoscopy and rectal biopsy: a survey of current UK practice. Eur J Gastroenterol Hepatol 1996;8(2):149-51
sources.supports: Postal survey of 277 UK consultant gastroenterologists: 71% of sigmoidoscopies were rigid; perforation in 5 of 328,815 rigid sigmoidoscopies (8 of 134,482 flexible); significant bleeding in 35 of 328,815 rigid; overall complication rate after sigmoidoscopy and rectal biopsy 0.01%

sources.name: Attenberger UI, Winter J, Harder FN, et al. Height of rectal cancer: a comparison between rectoscopic and different MRI measurements. Gastroenterol Res Pract 2020;2020:2130705
sources.supports: Rigid rectoscopy measured from the anal verge is the reference standard and most common method for rectal cancer height; UICC by rigid endoscopy: low up to 6 cm, mid 6-12 cm, high 12-16 cm; tumour height and relation to the peritoneal reflection matter for treatment; rigid rectoscopy has a low complication rate but is uncomfortable

partner.opening: Please perform a rigid sigmoidoscopy and proctoscopy for Mr Pryce on this manikin, talking me through what you're doing.

reveals.trigger: Asks for consent and offers a chaperone
reveals.finding: He agrees and would like a chaperone; a nurse is present.
No external haemorrhoids, fissure or skin tags.
Say: "You feel a hard, irregular edge at your fingertip on the posterior wall. There is blood on the glove."
Say: "Small internal haemorrhoids, not bleeding. The anal canal is otherwise normal."
Say: "An ulcerated, friable lesion on the posterior wall; its lower edge is 7 cm from the anal verge. The scope reaches 16 cm."

push.question: Why examine with your finger first?
push.expect: It must always come before rigid sigmoidoscopy: it finds a mass, stenosis, abscess or pain that changes the plan.

push.question: How far will you advance the sigmoidoscope?
push.expect: Only as far as the lumen can be seen without force; never force past the rectosigmoid; record the depth reached.

push.question: Why record the distance from the anal verge?
push.expect: It places a rectal cancer as low, mid or high rectum for treatment planning; record the wall position too.

curveballs.prompt: He is in severe pain on the rectal examination and you feel a tender, fluctuant swelling.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop: possible perirectal abscess. No instrumentation; senior review.

curveballs.prompt: You can't see the lumen at 12 cm.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Withdraw slightly, insufflate and re-angle; never push blind; stop if it still can't be seen.

curveballs.prompt: He asks you to stop halfway.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Stop at once, withdraw under vision and talk to him.
